span: ‘economic criteria’ for the purpose of Article 15 is permissible
why: Concerns economic-criteria reservation (EWS) under Article 15/16, not reservation in promotion for SC/ST.

span: Whether the Appellants are bound by the compensation as per the agreement under the Land Acquisition rules, and have waived off their right to seek enhanced compensation?
why: Frames a question about waiver of the right to enhanced compensation; no position stated in the passage.

span: the High Court has enhanced the amount of compensation to Rs.174/- per sq. ft.
why: Facts: the High Court enhanced compensation and BSNL appeals; the Supreme Court's view follows later.

span: this Court condoned the delay in filing the appeal as a large number of similarly situate persons have been granted relief by this Court
why: Describes an earlier land-acquisition enhancement appeal relied on by a party; the next paragraph says such decisions do not help, so the court does not adopt it.

span: the land owners shall be entitled to compensation at Rs.149/- per sq.yard at par with other land owners whose lands were acquired in the year 1982
why: Headnote holding: landowners are entitled to the enhanced compensation of Rs.149 per sq. yard, though the interest and statutory benefits for the delay are removed.

span: without any further analysis of evidence or discussion, abruptly enhanced the market rates of the acquired lands
why: Court criticises an unreasoned enhancement by the Tribunal and High Court but this passage does not state its outcome or deny the power to enhance.

span: The Reference Court enhanced the amount of compensation.
why: Procedural history of the acquisition appeals; no holding.

span: Appellants from both sides pleaded to enhance the compensation to Rs. 297/- per square yard
why: Headnote records the plea for enhancement; the court's ruling on it begins in the next passage.
